These are coordination mechanisms. The retrieved English candidates included Article 11 and also Article 57 (task force may coordinate/cooperate with other institutions), which is sufficient to answer Yes for a general ‘institutional network/coordination mechanism’ indicator. 4.2.rationale: Golden label is No, and the Indonesian text supports No for ‘gender equality education’ as a standalone prevention/education measure. 5.3.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly engages traditional/customary actors. Pasal 10 ayat (1) huruf g requires involving “pemuka adat” (customary leaders) along with religious leaders, community, etc. Pasal 11 huruf a requires prevention socialization by “mengoptimalkan peran lembaga adat, budaya, agama dan organisasi kemasyarakatan.” Pasal 58 huruf c also mentions preventing violence against children by optimizing the role of “lembaga adat.” The retrieved candidates for this indicator did not include Pasal 10 or Pasal 58, but they DID include Article 81(1) which mentions “nilai-nilai kearifan lokal” and strengthening community/religious organizations; however, that alone is weaker. The judge’s rationale says nothing explicitly describes engagement with traditional/cultural organizations/leaders; that is incorrect relative to the actual regulation (pemuka adat/lembaga adat are explicit). So the main issue is evaluation failure (and secondarily retrieval could have been better, but the policy clearly contains the engagement language).

6.2.evaluator_rationale: The text mentions prevention of human trafficking as part of efforts to protect women, and it provides special protection for child victims of trafficking, but it does not set out special protection measures specifically targeted at women victims of human trafficking.
